projetos.resumo: Python package measuring how El Niño drives the climate of Brazil's Center-West, with a WebMap dashboard that works offline.
descricao: Installable Python package (enso_co) that quantifies the teleconnection between the El Niño-Southern Oscillation and the climate of Brazil's Center-West at the municipal level. It combines NOAA/CPC's official RONI, ONI and SOI indices with CHIRPS precipitation and ERA5-Land temperature retrieved through Google Earth Engine.

It applies Bretherton autocorrelation correction, circular permutation tests and Moran's I. RONI is the primary index, following NOAA since February 2026. The output is a self-contained dashboard that works offline.
destaques: Robust latitudinal gradient: r between -0.836 and -0.849, with Moran's I above 0.93
Strong negative pole in northern Mato Grosso and an OND seasonal window identified empirically
All data retrieved programmatically, with no manual downloads

projetos.resumo: Serverless pipeline that processed 20 years of CHIRPS in Earth Engine to quantify the February 2026 climate disaster in Minas Gerais.
descricao: In February 2026, the Zona da Mata region of Minas Gerais faced an unprecedented climate disaster. This geospatial ETL pipeline filters 20 years (2006 to 2026) of daily CHIRPS imagery in Google Earth Engine, delegating the spatial reduction to Google's clusters.
GeoPandas harmonizes the 2024 IBGE boundaries, Pandas computes means, deviations and anomalies, and the result is injected into a self-contained Leaflet WebMap with no back-end.

projetos.resumo: DuckDB querying the 141 million buildings of Open Buildings in Brazil straight from S3, with a WebMap comparing Google and Microsoft.
descricao: Python pipeline that queries Google-Microsoft Open Buildings, with 2.5 billion buildings worldwide and 141 million in Brazil, straight from public S3 storage with DuckDB: Parquet reads with predicate pushdown and spatial SQL, with no server and no need to download the whole dataset for each analysis.

Areas of interest use the official polygons of the 2022 IBGE municipal boundaries, and new AOIs are added through a command-line tool that fetches the polygon from the IBGE API. The result is a multi-AOI WebMap with a three-tab panel: an overview with the Google × Microsoft split, a histogram of footprint areas by size class with a comparison table across AOIs, and the details of each clicked building.

descricao: Platform with three interactive modules aimed at the forestry sector. The first maps land use with MapBiomas Collection 10 (1985 to 2024) and isolates commercial plantations. The second detects dense forests by combining Sentinel-2 NDVI and NDII to separate forest stands from seasonal crops.

The third maps above-ground carbon stock with ESA CCI Biomass v6.0 (2015 to 2022). When you click the map, the app generates charts of the surrounding class composition, the monthly phenological cycle or the evolution of carbon per hectare.

projetos.resumo: A report factory: pipelines that generate technical PDF dossiers on rural registry, soils, climate and land use in minutes, not days.
descricao: Suite of pipelines that turns the production of technical reports, once manual and repetitive, into an automated system. It combines local processing with GeoPandas and Rasterio for sensitive vector data (CAR rural environmental registry, Legal Reserve, permanent preservation areas) with Google Earth Engine for nationwide analyses.

projetos.resumo: Python package comparing classical models and neural networks in dendrometry, inventory and U-Net tree crown segmentation.
descricao: Installable Python package (forestpy) that applies machine learning and deep learning to classic Forest Engineering problems: dendrometry, forest inventory, site classification, diameter distribution and remote sensing, up to semantic segmentation of tree crowns with a U-Net in PyTorch.

The central thesis is shown empirically across twelve sessions: no paradigm is universally superior. Classical models win with the right functional form or with little data; neural networks win with richer features or spatially dense outputs. The data are synthetic and reproducible, with realistic distributions of Eucalyptus grandis plantations.
destaques: The U-Net beats the NDVI baseline by +0.72 IoU in tree crown segmentation

Inspired by Vinicius Richter's fptools and extended to neural networks

projetos.resumo: Given a municipality, it returns the most similar ones by livestock profile: IBGE data become text, vectors and cosine similarity.
descricao: Content-based recommender system that answers a practical question: given a Brazilian municipality, which ones have the most similar agricultural profile? It helps, for example, a consultant in Cambuquira (MG) find analogous municipalities in other states for benchmarking or commercial expansion.

The pipeline downloads livestock herd data from the Municipal Livestock Survey (SIDRA, table 3939) and the territorial hierarchy from the Localidades API, derives low, medium or high activity profiles and each municipality's specialization, and combines everything into a document of tags. CountVectorizer, with the RSLP stemmer for Portuguese and keeping compound names intact, turns these documents into vectors; cosine similarity ranks the neighbors.

It is an original adaptation of the vector space project from chapter 8 of the Data Science Academy postgraduate program, swapping movies for municipalities, with a six-session tutorial and an optional spatial validation extension using Moran's index.
destaques: Query by name, by IBGE code or by a hypothetical tag profile
Each recommendation is explained: shared tokens and the three metrics side by side
Search for analogs outside the municipality's own state, for cross-state benchmarking

projetos.resumo: Serverless timber tally system: an offline-first field module and a client dashboard with log and firewood volume scaling.
descricao: Serverless front-end application that digitizes the collection, calculation and presentation of timber tallies for logs and firewood. The field module works offline, saves locally, computes volumes in real time and shrinks photos to lightweight base64 before export.

The whole state of a job becomes a single JSON file that feeds a public dashboard with indicators, Chart.js charts and a carousel of yard photos. The calculation engine applies Smalian's formula, tolerant to missing measurements, and converts firewood from stacked cubic meters (stere) to solid cubic meters.

projetos.resumo: Five lessons that take an uninstrumented service all the way to correlated metrics, traces and logs with OpenTelemetry.
descricao: Incremental journey through the modern observability ecosystem in Python. Starting from an intentionally uninstrumented application, each lesson adds a pillar: metrics with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus, distributed tracing with Tempo and W3C context propagation, structured logs correlated in Loki and instrumented PostgreSQL persistence.
Everything runs on the Grafana LGTM stack with Docker Compose. The repository documents how the code evolves through progressive commits and how the reasoning evolves through original study guides.

consultorias.intro: I provide geoprocessing and GIS development consulting for environmental licensing, power transmission lines and environmental compensation, currently as a consultant for Vimef Engenharia. Maps and analyses come out of Python pipelines built on official datasets and elevation models, ready to go into the technical report. Below are examples of real deliverables.

itens.local: Environmental licensing, IEF terms of reference
itens.resumo: Map sheets to the IEF standard: land use, sub-basins, vegetation types, preservation areas and engineering constraints.
descricao: Maps for the PCIA (compensation for environmental intervention) and the PRADA (recovery of degraded areas) of the 345 kV Jaguara–Araxá 3 C1 transmission line (Engie / Graúna Transmissora), which runs 58.4 km between Rifaina (SP), Sacramento and Araxá (MG). The line is framed within the ANA sub-basins (BHO) and the IBGE vegetation types, and the compensation areas, next to the Miranda hydropower plant on the Araguari River, get their own map sheets.

In the PRADA, land use and land cover come from MapBiomas Collection 9 (2023), clipped to the compensation areas for permanent preservation areas, threatened species and the Atlantic Forest. In the PCIA, the survey of permanent preservation areas combines FABDEM hillshade (30 m), flow accumulation, contour lines, the maximum flood level of 633.5 m and existing access roads, to avoid conflicts with the engineering design.
destaques: Every map sheet follows the IEF terms of reference (version of 12/01/2021)
A 118 ha property, with 19.9 ha delineated in three compensation areas
Maximum flood level and access roads overlaid with the permanent preservation area

itens.resumo: EMBRAPA slope classes from LiDAR or elevation models, with a statistics table and true 3D surface area.
entregaveis: Planimetric area and true 3D surface area
descricao: Slope analysis to support the delineation of terrain-based permanent preservation areas and the planning of interventions. Slope is computed in degrees (gdaldem slope), converted to percent and classified into the six EMBRAPA classes, from flat (0 to 3%) to escarpment (above 75%).

Each map sheet includes the full statistics table: planimetric area and true area considering the terrain, perimeter, minimum, maximum, mean, median, standard deviation and distribution by class. In the Antiga IB polygon, 1 m airborne LiDAR showed a mean slope of 35.1%, dominated by strongly rolling terrain; in Campina Verde, 12.5 m ALOS PALSAR indicated 42.4% of the area in rolling terrain.
destaques: Method documented on the map sheet itself, for auditing
In Antiga IB, the true 3D area is 8% larger than the planimetric area
The same methodology from 2.5 ha to 45 ha

descricao: Self-contained WebMap, in a single HTML file, built for the forestry suppression inventory of the 203 kV transmission line, with spans in Buri, Capão Bonito, Guapiara, Itaberá, Itapeva and Itararé (SP). It shows the eucalyptus and pine suppressed in each span, the 40 m corridor, the permanent preservation areas from the CAR registry and a Sentinel-2 mosaic from late March 2026 to check current conditions.

The team draws new polygons directly on the map: the area is computed on the spot, the totals by species update and the state is saved in the browser. At the end, everything is exported to GeoJSON, KML or a new WebMap for the client.
